title: Content Pack Manifest, Component Identity & Typed Payload Contract
objective: Establish the governed CNI content-pack manifest, stable component identity and typed payload contract needed for later dependency, narrative and cross-pack interoperability work.

scope.purpose: Create the first CNI pack/dependency foundation without taking authority from MIB-05, narrative, Action/Event or ARI owner domains.
scope.completion_gate: A deterministic content-pack manifest with stable component identity, independently selectable components, declared content domains, required/optional typed payload validation, ARI resource references and deterministic serialization compiles and round-trips through governed tooling without direct owner-domain mutation or duplicate resource identity.

selection_boundaries: ROADMAP_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH.json is the cross-program sequence authority and was reconsulted before successor selection.
MIB-05 remains source-pack compiler/linter/importer and compiled pack manifest authority; CNI-01 extends modular component/payload semantics without replacing it.
Pack registry remains pack release identity/install/dependency reference authority.
ARI remains resource identity, bytes/reference state, derivative lineage and rights/use-capability authority; CNI packs reference ARI resources rather than duplicating them.
CNI does not become canonical Story or owner-domain state authority.
Narrative/runtime changes bind to governed Actions/Events rather than directly mutate owner-domain state.
No dependency solver, narrative state runtime, dialogue runtime, sharing authority, provider activation, deployment, migration, PCA, SMB-08 or later CNI implementation was included.
CNI-01 implementation authority is retired after this completed_verified checkpoint.

plan_adjustments.change: Added encounters to the representative pack's declaredContentDomains; no production behavior changed.

plan_adjustments.change: Aligned the source-governance verifier with the existing runtime string representation and present governance phrases; no runtime or governance semantics changed.
